questions.stem: Which of the following is an example of fixed capital?
questions.explanation: Fixed capital includes long-term assets like machinery that are used over time, while cash, inventory, and receivables are considered circulating capital.

distractorRationale.a: b: Cash in hand is a short-term asset and part of circulating capital.
distractorRationale.b: c: Inventory is also a current asset and falls under circulating capital.
distractorRationale.c: d: Accounts receivable are short-term assets and not classified as fixed capital.

questions.stem: What is the primary purpose of calculating working capital?
questions.explanation: Calculating working capital helps businesses understand their short-term financial health by comparing current assets to current liabilities.

distractorRationale.a: a: Long-term profitability is assessed through different financial metrics, not working capital.
distractorRationale.b: c: Fixed asset investments are evaluated separately from working capital.
distractorRationale.c: d: Total revenue is not directly related to working capital calculations.

questions.stem: Which of the following is a source of long-term finance?
questions.explanation: Debentures are a form of long-term finance used by companies to raise capital, whereas the other options are typically short-term financing methods.

distractorRationale.a: a: A bank overdraft is a short-term borrowing option.
distractorRationale.b: b: Trade credit is also a short-term financing method.
distractorRationale.c: d: Short-term loans are not classified as long-term finance.
